# ast-grep(sg) ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting. ## What is ast-grep? ast-grep is an [abstract syntax tree](https://dev.to/balapriya/abstract-syntax-tree-ast-explained-in-plain-english-1h38) based tool to search code by pattern code. Think of it as your old-friend [`grep`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grep), but matching AST nodes instead of text. You can write patterns as if you are writing ordinary code. It will match all code that has the same syntactical structure. You can use `$` sign + upper case letters as a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildcard_character), e.g. `$MATCH`, to match any single AST node. Think of it as [regular expression dot](https://regexone.com/lesson/wildcards_dot) `.`, except it is not textual. Try the [online playground](https://ast-grep.github.io/playground.html) for a taste! ## Screenshot ![demo](https://ast-grep.github.io/image/search-replace.png) See more screenshots on the [website](https://ast-grep.github.io/). ## Installation You can install ast-grep from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise, or MacPorts: ```bash npm install --global @ast-grep/cli # `pnpm approve-builds` may be needed pip install ast-grep-cli brew install ast-grep cargo install ast-grep --locked cargo binstall ast-grep # install via scoop scoop install main/ast-grep # install via MacPorts sudo port install ast-grep # try ast-grep in nix-shell nix-shell -p ast-grep # try ast-grep with mise mise use -g ast-grep ``` [Packages](https://repology.org/project/ast-grep/versions) are available on other platforms too. ## Command line usage ast-grep has the following form: ```bash ast-grep --pattern 'var code = $PATTERN' --rewrite 'let code = new $PATTERN' --lang ts ``` ### Examples * Rewrite code using null coalescing operator: ```bash ast-grep -p '$A && $A()' -l ts -r '$A?.()' ``` * Rewrite Zodios code: ```bash ast-grep -p 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF as const,)' -l ts -r 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF)' -i ``` ## Features ast-grep helps you search and replace code based on abstract syntax trees. It can help you do lightweight static analysis and massive scale code manipulation in an intuitive way. Key features: * **Intuitive pattern syntax**: Write patterns that look like ordinary code you would write every day (the pattern is isomorphic to code). * **jQuery-like API**: For AST traversal and manipulation. * **YAML configuration**: Write new linting rules or code modifications using YAML. * **Fast and scalable**: Utilizes multiple cores for performance. * **Beautiful CLI**: User-friendly command line interface. ## Use Cases * **Open-source library authors**: Help your library users adopt breaking changes more easily. * **Tech leads**: Enforce code best practices tailored to your business needs. * **Security researchers**: Write security rules much faster. ## More Information Visit the [official website](https://ast-grep.github.io/) for complete documentation and tutorials. ## Schemas JSON schemas for ast-grep rule configuration are available in the `schemas/` directory. These schemas help you write valid ast-grep rules with IDE support.

function __fish_executable_global_optspecs
	string join \n c/config= h/help V/version
end

function __fish_executable_needs_command
	# Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
	set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
	set -e cmd[1]
	argparse -s (__fish_executable_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
	or return
	if set -q argv[1]
		# Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
		echo $argv[1]
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

function __fish_executable_using_subcommand
	set -l cmd (__fish_executable_needs_command)
	test -z "$cmd"
	and return 1
	contains -- $cmd[1] $argv
end

_ast-grep() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="ast__grep"
                ;;
            ast__grep,completions)
                cmd="ast__grep__subcmd__completions"
                ;;
            ast__grep,help)
                cmd="ast__grep__subcmd__help"
                ;;
            ast__grep,lsp)
                cmd="ast__grep__subcmd__lsp"
                ;;
            ast__grep,new)
                cmd="ast__grep__subcmd__new"
                ;;
# Print an optspec for argparse to handle cmd's options that are independent of any subcommand.
function __fish_ast_grep_global_optspecs
	string join \n c/config= h/help V/version
end

function __fish_ast_grep_needs_command
	# Figure out if the current invocation already has a command.
	set -l cmd (commandline -opc)
	set -e cmd[1]
	argparse -s (__fish_ast_grep_global_optspecs) -- $cmd 2>/dev/null
	or return
	if set -q argv[1]
		# Also print the command, so this can be used to figure out what it is.
		echo $argv[1]
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

def run(exe,args,cwd='/tmp',inp=None,env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)

 r,_,_=select.select([p.stdout],[],[],timeout)
 if not r: return None
 h=b''
 while not h.endswith(b'\r\n\r\n'):
  ch=p.stdout.read(1)
  if not ch: return None
  h+=ch
 length=int(h.decode().split(':',1)[1].split('\r')[0]); return json.loads(p.stdout.read(length))
def collect(n=100,timeout=1.5):
 out=[]
 for i in range(n):
  m=read_one(timeout if not out else 0.3)
  if m is None: break
  out.append(m)
  if m.get('method')=='client/registerCapability' and 'id' in m:

        new_text,applied=apply_edits(doc_text, build_edits_for_matches(matches))

def handle_interactive_rewrites(all_matches, opts, color=False, mode='run'):
    session=Interactive(); applied=0; accept_all=False; quit=False
    # group by file and apply accepted edits per file as we go (original applies each accepted before next prompt)
    for file_display,doc_text,matches in group_matches_by_file(all_matches):
        fs_path=matches[0].get('fs_path') if matches else None
        accepted_edits=[]
        for m in matches:
            if quit: break
            if m.get('replacement') is None: continue
            if accept_all:
                accepted_edits.append(m); continue
            # build single-edit diff content
            while True:
                new_text,_=apply_edits(doc_text, [(m['replacement_offsets'][0] if m.get('replacement_offsets') else m['node'].start, m['replacement_offsets'][1] if m.get('replacement_offsets') else m['node'].end, m['replacement'], m)])
                diff=make_diff(doc_text,new_text,color=False)
                title=''
                if m.get('rule') is not None:
                    title=f"{SEV_DISPLAY.get(m.get('severity'),m.get('severity'))}[{m['rule'].id}]: {m.get('message','')}\n"
                content=f"{file_display}\n{title}{diff}"
                ans=session.prompt(content,'rewrite')
                if ans=='y':
                    accepted_edits.append(m); break
                if ans=='n': break
                if ans=='a':
                    accept_all=True; accepted_edits.append(m); break
                if ans=='q':
                    quit=True; break
                if ans=='e':
                    edited=open_editor_for_text(m['replacement'])
                    # Editor file may end with newline added by editor; original likely trims trailing newline? Keep rstrip one trailing \n
                    if edited.endswith('\n'): edited=edited[:-1]
                    m['replacement']=edited; continue
            # end while
        # apply accepted for this file now
        if accepted_edits:
            new_text,applied=apply_edits(doc_text, build_edits_for_matches(accepted_edits))
            applied+=len(applied)
            if mode=='stdin':
                sys.stdout.write(new_text+"\n")
            elif fs_path:
                with open(fs_path,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='') as f: f.write(new_text)
        if quit:
            # Warning lines (colored if tty)
            if sys.stdout.isatty():
                sys.stdout.write("\x1b[33mWarning:\x1b[0m \x1b[1mInteractive editing exited.\x1b[0m\n\x1b[34mHelp:\x1b[0m Your accepted edit has been saved.\n")
            else:
                sys.stdout.write("Warning: Interactive editing exited.\nHelp: Your accepted edit has been saved.\n")
            return applied

        if sys.stdout.isatty(): sys.stdout.write(f"Applied {applied} changes\n")
        else: eprint(f"Applied {applied} changes\n")
    return applied
